label: Guangdong style
note: Influenced first by Hong Kong and later by Taiwanese play; a single parent arrow understates this. The late-1980s move to additive scoring is unsourced on the wiki.

label: Nanyang variants
note: Drawn with a dashed connector in the source chart: no source establishes this descent.

label: Filipino style
note: Sits under Nanyang despite a 16-tile hand resembling Taiwanese. The distinguishing test is that Filipino play treats winds and dragons as flowers.

label: Mainland regionals
note: These eleven nodes stand in for a hundred-plus real variants, most undocumented in English. The group began on a Chinese Classical frame and only later adopted HKOS's simplified scoring, so its placement under Hong Kong old style is a simplification.
